heard: The Nazca destroyed their ecosystem by clearing trees to carve giant lines. Intricate geoglyphs of animals stretched across more than 1,300 kilometers of dry plateau. Expanding maize and cotton agriculture required removing deep-rooted harongo trees. An El Nino event around 500 AD unleashed torrential coastal flooding. Without root systems, the unprotected soil washed away into deep river channels. Their aqueducts dried up, collapsing the civilization into desert. The Nazca destroyed their ecosystem by clearing trees to carve giant lines.
